derivation_notes: The refinement assumes irreversible endosomal degradation occurs predominantly from the immature or degradative fraction E - M before receptors acquire recycling competence. This preserves the same states and target equation but changes the E and M balance laws so maturation and degradation directly compete on the immature pool.
change_summary: The uniform endosomal degradation assumption is relaxed: degradation now drains the immature subpool E - M instead of total E and mature M separately. This creates stronger composition-dependent delay in surface recovery when endosomal load is present mainly as immature receptor.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Endosomal degradation acts uniformly on the total endosomal pool regardless of maturation or sorting state.
assumption_audit.mechanism: State-specific endosomal sorting in which receptors are preferentially degraded before or instead of entering the recycling-competent compartment.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The parent is approximately recovered when M tracks E closely so that E - M remains negligible over the observed interval, making degradation of the immature-only fraction effectively indistinguishable from uniform endosomal degradation.

response_change.parent_relation: The recycling contribution to dS_dt depends only on the mature recycling-competent pool M and available capacity R, so at fixed R the surface recovery rises with a single saturating phase as M increases.
response_change.child_relation: Make the endosomal degradation loss borne specifically by the degradative/immature fraction E-M rather than by total E, so maturation competes more directly with loss. Then dS_dt as a function of internalized load acquires stronger curvature because increasing E can first feed M and later be diverted into degradation before maturation, especially when M is still small.
response_change.observable_effect: After a production change that generates a transiently large immature endosomal pool, surface recovery is more delayed and more load-sensitive than in the parent: for similar E but lower M/E, dS_dt stays lower because more receptor is lost before becoming recyclable.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when a substantial immature endosomal fraction exists, i.e. E-M is not negligible relative to E, such as early after increased internalization or when endosomal_maturation_rate is comparable to or slower than endosomal_degradation_rate.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training regimes with modest delay, the same mechanism appears as a mild lag in surface recovery after endosomal loading; in extended holdout regimes with larger transient immature pools, the stronger pre-maturation loss produces a more pronounced reduction in dS_dt that the parent cannot match with one parameter set.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where degradation acts effectively uniformly across endosomal subpools, or approximately when M tracks E closely so that E-M stays negligible over the observed interval.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Preferential degradation of the immature endosomal receptor fraction before recycling competence is acquired
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: State-specific endosomal sorting in which receptors are more likely to be degraded before or instead of maturing into the recycling-competent compartment, so degradation primarily drains the immature/degradative subpool E-M.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the degradation loss now depends jointly on two declared states through E-M, so the same total endosomal load can imply different future surface recovery depending on composition. A single retuned first-order degradation coefficient on E cannot generate this composition-sensitive curvature while preserving later recovery once M has matured.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Uniform first-order endosomal degradation removes receptor from total E and from M with the same state-independent law.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Degradation predominantly removes the immature/degradative subpool E-M, making maturation and degradation compete for the same substrate.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is approximately recovered when E-M remains small because M closely tracks E, so immature-specific degradation becomes observationally close to uniform endosomal degradation.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For trajectories observed under the same fixed parameter set, compare cases with similar E and R but different immature_pool E-M. The child predicts lower subsequent recycling support and slower surface recovery when mature_fraction M/E is lower, whereas the parent's uniform degradation cannot create as strong a composition-dependent suppression without also distorting trajectories after M catches up.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all existing parent parameters cannot absorb this across both low- and high-immature-fraction conditions with one shared parameter set because the parent only scales degradation with E and M through fixed separate linear losses. It lacks the specific competitive coupling on E-M, so matching delayed recovery for immature-rich trajectories would force degradation or maturation changes that also mispredict trajectories where most endosomal receptor is already mature.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when a substantial immature endosomal fraction exists, i.e. E-M is not negligible relative to E, such as early after increased internalization or when endosomal_maturation_rate is comparable to or slower than endosomal_degradation_rate.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training regimes with modest delay, the same mechanism appears as a mild lag in surface recovery after endosomal loading; in extended holdout regimes with larger transient immature pools, the stronger pre-maturation loss produces a more pronounced reduction in dS_dt that the parent cannot match with one parameter set.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where degradation acts effectively uniformly across endosomal subpools, or approximately when M tracks E closely so that E-M stays negligible over the observed interval.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model currently degrades the entire endosomal pool E at one uniform first-order rate even though only the immature/non-recycling-sorted fraction should be preferentially committed to degradative routing before gaining recycling competence.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the parent assumption that endosomal degradation acts uniformly on total endosomal abundance regardless of maturation/sorting state.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: State-specific endosomal sorting in which receptors are more likely to be degraded before or instead of maturing into the recycling-competent compartment, so degradation primarily drains the immature/degradative subpool E-M.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to make degradation compete with maturation on the immature endosomal pool rather than remove receptors uniformly from all of E. The parent target mapping for dS_dt has a single-phase dependence on endosomal history: once M and R are specified, only one saturating recycling law controls return to the surface, and the way E feeds future dS_dt is too simple because total endosomal loss ignores whether receptors have matured. Vary the post-perturbation endosomal composition through conditions that generate different immature fractions E-M while holding the same production, internalization, recycling, and capacity parameters fixed. Under those admissible conditions, the child predicts lower subsequent dS_dt for trajectories with larger immature load because more receptor is degraded before entering M; the parent can only mimic this by changing global rates, which would also alter later recovery when M has caught up. This is a target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory change, because the altered competition changes how observed E and M jointly imply future surface recovery through their effect on the recyclable pool. The contrast is most visible when initialization or perturbation leaves M well below E and maturation is not much faster than degradation; if M approximately equals E throughout observation, the refinement is weak and the parent is effectively recovered.

scenario_text: This scenario models the surface abundance of a signaling receptor after a change in receptor production. Surface receptors are internalized into an endosomal compartment, where some return to the plasma membrane and the remainder are removed. The surface and endosomal receptor pools are jointly evolved over time, with production treated as a fixed cellular background rate.
